knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=Specifies sequence type, typically "DNA" or "AA" ;; min.pct=Minimum relative abundance percentage threshold to filter out low-frequency haplotypes in GetQSData ;; q=Order of the diversity index or entropy (used in Hill, Renyi, HCq, RaoPow) ;; size=Total number of reads in the downsampled sample prior to abundance filtering in DSFT ;; p.cut=Abundance threshold in the filter for DSFT ;; conf=Level of confidence in trimming haplotypes, defaults to 0.95 in DSFT ;; off=Offset for position numbering in SummaryMuts
- alternatives: Biostrings::readDNAStringSet is preferred over ReadAmplSeqs for reading raw fasta files without frequency information before collapsing them with Collapse ;; DNA.dist from the ape package is used to compute genetic distances before calculating functional diversity or genotyping
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing amplicon NGS data from highly variable populations like viral quasispecies, 16S/18S ribosomal metagenomics, or tumor genetic diversity, especially when you need to correct for sample size bias or sequencing errors before computing diversity indices.
- pitfalls: Comparing diversity indices directly between samples with different coverages/sample sizes can lead to severe bias; use DSFT (Downsampling and Fringe Trimming) to correct for this. Traditional ecological correction methods fail on NGS data because they rely on low-frequency haplotypes that are typically removed as technical noise; DSFT is specifically designed to handle this. ConsSeq does not consider IUPAC ambiguity codes and resolves ties randomly.

workflows.name: collapse_and_correct_gaps_ns
workflows.intent: Load raw amplicon reads, collapse them to unique haplotypes with frequencies, correct gaps and indeterminate bases (Ns) against a reference sequence, and recollapse to update frequencies.
input: Toy.GapsAndNs.fna (FASTA file of raw amplicon reads containing gaps or Ns)
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw sequences using readDNAStringSet ;; 2. Collapse reads to unique haplotypes and frequencies using Collapse ;; 3. Correct gaps and Ns against a reference sequence (e.g., dominant haplotype) using CorrectGapsAndNs ;; 4. Recollapse the corrected sequences to update frequencies using Recollapse
workflows.code:
filepath<-system.file("extdata","Toy.GapsAndNs.fna", package="QSutils")
reads <- readDNAStringSet(filepath)
lstCollapsed <- Collapse(reads)
lstCorrected<-CorrectGapsAndNs(lstCollapsed$hseqs[2:length(lstCollapsed$hseqs)],
                lstCollapsed$hseqs[[1]])
lstCorrected<- c(lstCollapsed$hseqs[1],lstCorrected)
lstRecollapsed<-Recollapse(lstCorrected,lstCollapsed$nr)

workflows.name: strand_haplotype_intersection
workflows.intent: Filter and intersect haplotypes from forward and reverse sequencing strands to reduce sequencing errors.
workflows.stages: 1. Load forward and reverse amplicon sequences using ReadAmplSeqs ;; 2. Intersect and filter strand haplotypes using IntersectStrandHpls
workflows.code:
filepath<-system.file("extdata","ToyData_FWReads.fna", package="QSutils")
lstFW <- ReadAmplSeqs(filepath,type="DNA")
filepath<-system.file("extdata","ToyData_RVReads.fna", package="QSutils")
lstRV <- ReadAmplSeqs(filepath,type="DNA")
lstI <- IntersectStrandHpls(lstFW$nr,lstFW$hseqs,lstRV$nr,lstRV$hseqs)

workflows.name: quasispecies_diversity_analysis
workflows.intent: Compute incidence-based, abundance-based, and functional diversity indices to characterize quasispecies complexity, with sample size correction.
input: ToyData_10_50_1000.fna (FASTA file with haplotype and frequency headers)
workflows.stages: 1. Load quasispecies data using ReadAmplSeqs ;; 2. Compute incidence-based indices (SegSites, TotalMutations) ;; 3. Compute abundance-based indices (Shannon, GiniSimpson, Hill, Renyi, HCq) ;; 4. Compute functional diversity indices using genetic distances (MutationFreq, FAD, NucleotideDiversity, RaoPow) ;; 5. Correct for sample size bias using DSFT
workflows.code:
filepath<-system.file("extdata","ToyData_10_50_1000.fna", package="QSutils")
lst <- ReadAmplSeqs(filepath,type="DNA")
length(lst$hseqs)
SegSites(lst$hseqs)
TotalMutations(lst$hseqs)
Shannon(lst$nr)
NormShannon(lst$nr)
ShannonVar(lst$nr)
NormShannonVar(lst$nr)
GiniSimpson(lst$nr)
GiniSimpsonMVUE(lst$nr)
GiniSimpsonVar(lst$nr)
Hill(lst$nr,q=1)
HillProfile(lst$nr)
Renyi(lst$nr,q=3)
RenyiProfile(lst$nr)
HCq(lst$nr, q= 4)
HCqVar(lst$nr, q= 4)
HCqProfile(lst$nr)
dst <- DNA.dist(lst$hseqs,model="raw")
MutationFreq(dst)
FAD(dst)
NucleotideDiversity(dst)
nm <- nmismatch(pairwiseAlignment(lst$hseqs,lst$hseqs[1]))
MutationFreq(nm=nm,nr=lst$nr,len=width(lst$hseqs)[1])
MutationFreqVar(nm,lst$nr,len=width(lst$hseqs)[1])
NucleotideDiversity(dst,lst$nr)
RaoPow(dst,4,lst$nr)
RaoVar(dst,lst$nr)
RaoPowProfile(dst,lst$nr)
DSFT(lst$nr,size=2000)

workflows.name: genotyping_unknown_haplotypes
workflows.intent: Classify an unknown target haplotype into a genotype using reference standards and distance-based discriminant rules.
workflows.stages: 1. Load target sequence and reference sequences using ReadAmplSeqs ;; 2. Compute distance matrix using DNA.dist from ape ;; 3. Extract distances between references and from target to references ;; 4. Classify the target sequence using DBrule
workflows.code:
filepath<-system.file("extdata","Unknown-Genotype.fna", package="QSutils")
lst2Geno <- ReadAmplSeqs(filepath,type="DNA")
hseq <- lst2Geno$hseq[1]
filepath<-system.file("extdata","GenotypeStandards_A-H.fas", package="QSutils")
lstRefs <- ReadAmplSeqs(filepath,type="DNA")
RefSeqs <- lstRefs$hseq
dm <- as.matrix(DNA.dist(c(hseq,RefSeqs),model="K80"))
dgrp <- dm[-1,-1]
d <- dm[1,-1]
grp <- factor(substr(rownames(dgrp),1,1))
hr <- as.integer(grp)
dsc <- DBrule(dgrp,hr,d,levels(grp))
